taskTitle: Architecture review remediation — CI guard soundness, pgBackRest 2.50 version parity, and WAL backlog monitoring

notCaptured: df -B1 <PGDATA> — the denominator for NORAMEDI_OPSCHECK_PITR_MAX_WAL_BYTES. Still required before repo2 activation.

versionParity.question: repo1 healthy + repo2 unreachable: what does archive-push return, does PostgreSQL keep accepting foreground writes, does archived_count freeze, does failed_count increase, does a .ready backlog appear, does WAL disk usage increase, and does the backlog drain after repo2 recovery?
versionParity.method: Both arms run the same harness with the same topology, config and injection; the ONLY variable is the pgBackRest build. Pins resolve through apt-archive.postgresql.org and are re-verified against the running binary before the experiment starts; an unresolvable pin fails the build (PGBACKREST_PIN_UNAVAILABLE, exit 3) with no fallback.

comparison.note: absolute values differ (36 vs 3); that is retry cadence, not semantics

comparison.v250: REFUSED — ERROR [072] backup command must be run on the repository host

findings.statement: The pgBackRest suite's unsafe-cleanup guard was a negated pipeline under `set -o pipefail`. `grep -q` exits 0 on first match without draining stdin, the upstream `grep -v` then takes SIGPIPE and exits 141, pipefail promotes 141 to the pipeline status, and the leading `!` inverts that into success — so the guard reported CLEAN on precisely the input that contains the defect.
findings.consequence: Not merely a broken fixture. A real reintroduction of `rm -rf ... 2>/dev/null || true` into the restore drill could have been reported clean by the same race. Three sibling guards had the identical shape, two of them HIGH pg_hba security guards on the disposable cluster.
findings.evidence: CI run 31952565128 on ubuntu-latest: 217 passed / 1 failed on the mutation control, against a tree that was 216 / 0 locally. Reproduced deterministically: with the defect on line 1 of a ~1.5 MB haystack the old implementation reports CLEAN 3/3 and the new one detects it 3/3; the raw pipeline status is 141 under pipefail and 0 without it.
findings.resolution: Guards materialise the haystack and grep it directly, so the verdict is grep's own exit status. No mutation assertion weakened, deleted, or had an expected string edited. A permanent non-vacuous control was added, including the negative case (the same oversized haystack without the defect still passes).

findings.statement: On pgBackRest 2.50, `backup --repo=2` invoked on the PostgreSQL host with `repo2-host` configured is refused: ERROR: [072]: backup command must be run on the repository host. The identical topology and command succeed on 2.59.0.
findings.consequence: noramedi-pgbackrest-backup.sh --repo 2 runs on the primary, so runbook §22.11 CHECKPOINT 7 as published cannot succeed on production's current build. Initiating the backup on the repository host instead requires SSH trust in the repo-host -> production direction, which §16.5 forbids and §22.9's one-way trust deliberately does not create.
findings.evidence: Both arms of the A/B above: repo2BaseBackupInitiatedFrom = repo-host and reverseSshTrustRequired = true on 2.50; pg-host and false on 2.59.0. Same PostgreSQL image, same docker engine, same config.
findings.resolution: REPORTED, NOT RESOLVED. Recorded as a blocker in runbook §22.11 with the two options stated in §22.4a (upgrade pgBackRest first, or revisit the trust model — a security decision). Neither is authorized by this task and production was not touched.

findings.statement: The archive-push failure semantics are the same on 2.50 as on 2.59.0: the command FAILS, archived_count freezes, failed_count rises, a .ready backlog appears, pg_wal grows, PostgreSQL keeps accepting foreground writes, and the backlog fully drains once repo2 returns with zero acknowledged commits lost.
findings.consequence: The catastrophic silent-hole outcome does not occur on production's build either. The risk remains observable disk growth rather than undetectable data loss — which is exactly what R1-F4's monitoring is for.
findings.evidence: See versionParity.comparison; every semantic property matches. Only failed_count magnitude differs (36 vs 3), which is retry cadence.

findings.statement: No production signal measured pg_wal byte consumption or the pg_wal/archive_status/*.ready backlog. failedCount cannot express how much WAL is un-archived, lastArchivedAgeMinutes measures time rather than volume, and the disk check reads / as a percentage and names the wrong subsystem when it trips.
findings.consequence: repo2 activation would have proceeded with no way to observe the accumulation that Gate 0 identified as the failure mode.
findings.resolution: archive.walBytes and archive.readyCount added as OPTIONAL fields on the same schemaVersion 1 document, read via pg_ls_waldir() and pg_ls_dir('pg_wal/archive_status') so they resolve relative to the data directory PostgreSQL is actually running on. Neither reads WAL content. Unmeasurable is published as ABSENT, never 0. Three opscheck knobs, all off by default, with the activation gate refusing to start (exit 64) if repo2 is activated while either limit is 0.

findings.statement: The first 2.50 run classified INDETERMINATE on a healthy experiment: 102,500 rows committed and zero archive attempts across the whole outage, because repeat(md5(...),256) is almost perfectly compressible and archive_timeout=300 is longer than smoke mode's 180-second window, so no segment completed inside it.
findings.consequence: A version-parity experiment that silently answers "indeterminate" for a reason unrelated to pgBackRest is worse than no experiment, because the null result reads as a property of the build.
findings.resolution: The harness forces a WAL switch every 15 s (NORAMEDI_GATE0_WAL_SWITCH_INTERVAL) — the same mechanism archive_timeout already uses in production, run faster. It changes when segments are produced, not what archive-push does with one.

signals.source: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_ls_dir('pg_wal/archive_status') AS f WHERE f LIKE '%.ready'

walBacklogMonitoring.pgdataDerivation: Both are pg_catalog functions that resolve relative to the data directory PostgreSQL itself is running on. No PGDATA is hardcoded, derived from a version-specific path, or discovered by walking the filesystem.
walBacklogMonitoring.privacy: Neither reads WAL content. pg_ls_waldir() returns segment names and sizes; pg_ls_dir returns marker filenames. No segment is opened, so no tuple, no patient row and no secret is observable through this path. Only a byte total and a count leave the query.
walBacklogMonitoring.unmeasurableSemantics: ABSENT, never 0. A 0 would read as "no backlog" during exactly the outage these fields exist to detect.

thresholds.justification: 32 segments is approximately 512 MiB at the 16 MiB default segment size. At production archive_timeout=5min an idle cluster needs ~2.7h of total archive outage to reach it, i.e. after the existing 120-minute archived-WAL-age assertion has already fired; under write load it is reached in minutes, which is the case the age assertion misses. Gate 0 measured .ready rising 1 -> 12 in 180s at an accelerated synthetic rate, so the signal is monotonic rather than spiky. opscheck runs every 5 minutes, so a single sample over the limit is already a sustained condition.

DELIBERATELY has no non-zero default. The safe value is a function of free space on the PGDATA filesystem, which this repository has never measured on disklinik-prod-01; root at ~13% used is a percentage, not a denominator, and df -B1 <PGDATA> was not captured at preflight. Runbook §22.4a requires the operator to measure it and set no more than 25% of available bytes, recording the df output alongside the value. The 25% is a stated headroom convention, not a measurement.

The activation gate. Makes both limits and both measurements mandatory. With it true and either limit still 0, opscheck refuses to start (exit 64) at startup rather than failing at check time, because activating repo2 with a monitor that cannot see WAL backlog is a configuration error and must not be mistakable for a transient alert. Validated as a strict true/false enum so a typo cannot silently disable it.

alerting.note: F6 observability remains future work and is not started here.

walBacklogMonitoring.failureBehaviour: A configured limit with a missing or unreadable measurement is a FAILURE, never a pass. Enabling a check and then being unable to take its measurement is the silent-green this document exists to prevent.

backwardCompatibility.result: unchanged; the extra fields are ignored

walBacklogMonitoring.deploymentOrder: Deploy noramedi-pgbackrest-status.sh before setting any limit.

securityImpact: No new endpoint, credential, surface or subprocessor. The two new signals are aggregates read through pg_catalog and cannot expose WAL content, patient data or a secret. Three shell guards were made sound, two of which are HIGH pg_hba security guards that could previously report clean on a file containing the defect they exist to catch.
tenantIsolationImpact: None. No tenant-scoped code path is touched.
kvkkImpact: Neutral to positive. No new processing of personal or special-category data; the new measurements are a byte count and a file count. The seven runbook §16.2 legal prerequisites remain unmet and are unaffected.
migration: NONE. No schema change, no Prisma migration.
